blocks.title: What Your {{ AI Intake Agent }} Runs
blocks.description: Legal intake automation across the whole path: first ring, triage, conflict pre-check, consult, retainer.

cards.title: After-Hours Answering
cards.description: Calls that land at 9pm or during a deposition get answered on the first ring. The caller reaches an agent that takes the details.

cards.title: Case-Type Triage
cards.description: Personal injury, family, criminal, immigration, estate. The agent reads the matter type from the caller's own words and routes it down the path your firm set.

cards.title: Practice-Area Questions
cards.description: Each practice area asks different things. The agent runs the question set your attorneys wrote and stops once the consult has what it needs.

cards.title: Conflict Pre-Check
cards.description: Names and opposing parties go against your case management system before a consult is offered. Anything questionable waits for a human.

cards.title: Incident Date Flagging
cards.description: The agent records when the incident happened and flags it against the window your firm configured. It reports the date, and does not interpret the deadline.

cards.title: Consult Booking
cards.description: Availability comes from the right attorney's calendar, filtered by matter type. Real slots, booked, with the summary written before the consult.

cards.title: Document Follow-Up
cards.description: Police reports, medical records, photographs, prior filings. The agent asks for what the matter needs and keeps asking until the file arrives.

cards.title: Retainer Dispatch
cards.description: The e-sign link goes out inside the same conversation, not the next business day. Your intake lead sees which retainers are still open.

rows.leftDescription: Your attorneys are in a hearing and the phone rolls to voicemail. The caller has three firms to try.
rows.rightDescription: First ring, every time. Voicemail stops being part of your intake.

rows.leftDescription: A personal injury inquiry goes to three firms inside an hour. The one that books a consult gets the meeting.
rows.rightDescription: Your agent answers as the inquiry arrives, asks the qualifying questions, and offers a slot while the client is still reading.

rows.leftDescription: Half-hour consults on matters outside your practice areas or your jurisdiction. Attorney time nobody bills.
rows.rightDescription: Your criteria run before the calendar opens: case type, jurisdiction, incident date, the questions your attorneys ask first.

rows.leftDescription: Notes get typed up next morning, if someone gets to it. Names misspelled, conflicts checked late.
rows.rightDescription: Every answer lands in your case management system as a structured field, and the attorney opens a complete summary.

rows.leftDescription: The engagement letter goes out, the client gets busy, and the matter quietly dies.
rows.rightDescription: The agent keeps asking, on the schedule you set, until the signature lands or the client says no.

items.question: How is this different from a law firm answering service?
items.answer: An answering service takes a message, and your intake lead still calls back, qualifies and books. The agent completes the intake: your practice-area questions, a conflict pre-check against your own system, a consult in the right calendar, a structured summary.

items.question: What does the agent handle, and does it ever give legal advice?
items.answer: No legal advice. The agent gathers facts, screens against your criteria, books the consult, chases documents and signatures, re-books no-shows and routes declined matters to your referral list. Case value, strategy and representation belong to the attorney at the consult.

items.question: How does the conflict pre-check work?
items.answer: The agent screens the caller, opposing parties and matter references against your case management system while the conversation is open. A clean screen lets it offer times. Anything that looks like a hit goes to a human, and it never clears a conflict.

items.question: Does it work for our practice areas?
items.answer: Intake follows the same shape across personal injury, family, criminal, immigration and estate work: identify the matter, ask that area's questions, screen conflicts, book the consult. Only the question sets and the routing change, and your own attorneys write both.

items.question: What does faster response do to our signed-case rate?
items.answer: It changes which firm gets the conversation at all. Response time is what the figures above measure. The link from that to signed cases is firm-specific, and we publish no legal number here, because there is not one yet with a source behind it.

items.question: How long does deployment take?
items.answer: Between 5 and 15 days. Most of that is your input: which practice areas, which questions, which conflict rules. The build itself is a template plus integrations, and we test it against real inquiries before the agent answers a client of yours.

items.question: How do credits map to calls and messages?
items.answer: Credits are spent per resolved conversation and per minute of voice, so a quiet month costs less than a busy one. Signup credits do not expire. Client intake software for attorneys is often a seat licence; here the cost follows intake volume.

items.question: Who owns the intake data and the recordings?
items.answer: Your firm does. Transcripts, recordings and the records the agent writes belong to your account, and you can export or delete them. Retention windows are yours to set, and access is scoped per user, so intake staff see only the fields they need.

items.question: Can it extend past intake into matter updates and payment reminders?
items.answer: Yes. The same canvas runs status updates for existing clients, document chasing mid-matter and invoice reminders through your payment tool. Most firms start with after-hours intake and widen from there. The conversational AI platform page covers how the layers fit together.
